FAQ

Answers,
upfront.

The questions parents, teachers and judges ask first — condensed. For the full technical writeup, see the project report.

?

Do I need to learn a new keyboard?

No. The six keys map to the six Braille dots a student already knows — dot 1 types A, dots 1+2 type B, dots 1+4 type C.

?

Does it work in Bangla?

Yes. A Shift-based system unlocks Bangla vowel signs, numbers, punctuation and math from the same six keys.

?

How does the teacher read it?

Output streams over USB Serial into the Teacher Software, appearing as ordinary text in real time.

?

Does the student need Braille paper?

No. Nothing is embossed — chords are translated straight into digital text.

?

What does it run on?

An ESP32 reads each chord within a 180 ms window and sends it over Bluetooth and USB Serial at once.

?

How much does it cost?

Under $15 in parts — a fraction of the $700–800 a mechanical Brailler can run.

BILINGUAL BRAILLE SYSTEM
BrailleBridge
"Write in Braille. Read in real time."

A low-cost, bilingual digital Braille writing and classroom examination system. Students type independently in English or Bangla; teachers see plain, readable text appear as they write.

01 — WHY BRAILLEBRIDGE

Every other option
asks for a trade-off.

A slate & stylus is affordable but slow, fiddly, and easy to lose parts of. A Perkins Brailler is familiar but bulky, heavy, loud — and costs $700–800. A sighted writer is always available, but costs privacy and independence. BrailleBridge asks for none of those trade-offs.

Slate & stylus — manual, parts get lost
→
One key set, nothing to lose
Perkins Brailler — bulky, loud, $700–800
→
Pocket-sized, under $15 in parts
Sighted writer — no privacy, no control
→
Types independently, in private
Embossed Braille — teacher can't read it
→
Teacher sees plain text, instantly
THE PURPOSE

Protect Braille.
Remove the barrier.

BrailleBridge doesn't replace Braille — it keeps Braille as the student's natural way of writing, and simply removes the wall between what a blind student writes and what a sighted teacher can read.

02 — WHAT MAKES IT UNIQUE

One chord. Two
languages. Two outputs.

No existing product combines a six-dot chorded keyboard, English-and-Bangla translation, Bluetooth output and live teacher software in one affordable device.

True six-dot chording

Dot 1 makes A, dots 1+2 make B, dots 1+4 make C — the same combinations a Braille reader already knows.

Bilingual from one keyboard

Shift unlocks Bangla vowel signs, numbers, punctuation and math from the same six keys — no second device.

Dual live output

Bluetooth HID reaches the student's own device; USB Serial feeds the Teacher Software — simultaneously, every chord.

Working prototype — 3D-printed enclosure, ESP32 + Outemu switches
